quotes.text: Robotic process automation is software that does the copying a person would otherwise do, driving the same screens and the same keystrokes in the same order.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear one-sentence definition of RPA for beginners.

quotes.text: This is not a way to fix a messy process. It's a way to copy a tidy one, and it stays reliable only for as long as the tidy version of that process holds up in practice.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the central limit of RPA as a memorable rule.

quotes.text: The first mistake is automating something that should have been deleted. A bad process that runs by hand is annoying and visible, while the same process behind a bot runs faster, fails more quietly, and becomes much harder to argue with.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Warns against automating bad processes with a concrete contrast.

quotes.text: Real automation usually uses both with a cloud flow starting the work and a desktop flow finishing it on an older system.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains how cloud and desktop flows work together in Power Automate.

quotes.text: The skill worth building here has nothing to do with building bots. It's the ability to spot bot shaped work and describe it clearly enough that someone else can take it and act on it.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives practical career advice that outlasts any specific tool.

takeaways: RPA is software that copies a person's clicks and keystrokes across existing screens; it follows rules literally and is not artificial intelligence.

Bots shine on frequent, rule-based work with clean, structured data, but they break on free text, exceptions and small interface changes, and most automation programs stall for process and ownership reasons.
In Microsoft 365 the RPA tool is Power Automate: cloud flows connect services, desktop flows drive older applications, and unattended bots are licensed per bot.
hook: Every week someone retypes the same numbers from one screen into another, and software can now do that job. This beginner-friendly episode explains what robotic process automation really does, where it breaks, and how Power Automate brings it into Microsoft 365, so you can spot which of your own tasks a bot should take.
